title: Canonical affine envelope with its induced descent datum
statement:
Let $p:A\to B$ be a flat surjective morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], with $A=\operatorname{Spec}S$. Let $f:V\to A$ be quasi-affine [def-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism], meaning that the inverse image of each affine open is a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme. Let $\phi$ be a descent datum on $V$ over $A/B$ [def-pd-descent-datum]. Put $C=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and give $W$ the map to $A$ induced by $f^\sharp:S\to C$. Let $j:V\to W$ be the canonical morphism corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_C$ under [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. Then $V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $W\to A$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and $j$ is an open immersion over $A$ [def-weil-open-immersion].

Write $A_2=A\times_B A$, with projections $p_i$, and $V_i=V\times_{A,p_i}A_2$, $W_i=W\times_{A,p_i}A_2$ for $i=0,1$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. With $S_2=\Gamma(A_2,\mathcal O_{A_2})$, the maps $\beta_i:C\otimes_{S,p_i^\sharp}S_2\to\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal O_{V_i})$, $c\otimes t\mapsto c|_{V_i}\,t|_{V_i}$, are isomorphisms. The resulting identifications $\alpha_i:W_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal O_{V_i})$ identify the pullbacks $j_i$ of $j$ with the canonical morphisms to these spectra. The isomorphism
$$\psi=\alpha_1^{-1}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\phi^\sharp)\circ\alpha_0:W_0\xrightarrow{\sim}W_1,$$
where $\phi^\sharp:\Gamma(V_1,\mathcal O)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(V_0,\mathcal O)$, is over $A_2$ and satisfies $\psi\circ j_0=j_1\circ\phi$. On $A_3=A\times_B A\times_B A$, its pullbacks satisfy $\psi_{02}=\psi_{12}\circ\psi_{01}$, so $\psi$ is a descent datum on $W$ and $j$ intertwines the two data. The comparisons $\beta_i$ are natural for the pullbacks of $\phi$ to $A_3$ and agree with successive flat base change: under these comparisons $(c\otimes s)\otimes t$ corresponds to the product of the three pulled-back sections. No finite-presentation assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0247, lemma-quasi-affine, proof, second paragraph: canonical affine envelope, flat-base-change display, induced algebra isomorphism and its cocycle; returned proof steps 3 (envelope part), 4, 5 and 6

proof.text: Apply the canonical quasi-affine embedding over the affine base. The source is qcqs, the adjunction unit is open and lies over A, and its affine envelope maps affinely to A.

Specialize the qcqs flat global-sections theorem to whole opens. Identify its pushout comparison with comparison using the pushout universal property. The spectrum of the ring pushout is the affine pullback; check both projections to identify spectrumComparison. Its inverse alpha identifies the base-changed unit with the adjunction unit.

Prove the pure-tensor product formula by the two pushout inclusion equations. Prove naturality by pushout hom-ext and functoriality of sections. Naturality and preservation of isomorphisms by pushout show that flat affine base change preserves isomorphisms on global sections between quasi-affine sources.

For successive base change, use the proved quasi-affine base-change theorem. Apply the flat comparison again. Both generator formulas agree by the two projections of the pullback-pasting isomorphism and associativity of multiplication.

Represent the original datum by its universal transport V times_B A to V. The map from this pullback to W times_B A induces an isomorphism on global sections by flat base change. Extend the universal transport followed by the unit uniquely to the affine W times_B A using the inverse section map and Spec. Its structure-map identity follows by uniqueness. Evaluating it on pullback lifts defines natural transport on W, intertwining the given datum on every test scheme.

Prove identity after precomposing with the unit, whose section map is invertible. For the cocycle use the universal pair of successive pullbacks W times_B A times_B A. The corresponding map from V times_B A times_B A again has invertible section map, by naturality of the flat comparison. After precomposition the desired identity is exactly the original transport cocycle. Naturality pulls the universal equation back to arbitrary test points.

Evaluate transport naturality on the universal point of V times_A T to see that transitions intertwine unitBaseChange. On a flat affine overlap its section map is invertible, so affine-target uniqueness determines the envelope transition. The alpha unit identity and naturality of toSpecGamma identify this unique extension with the stated alpha conjugation.

lean.statement: theorem exists_descentDatum {A B V : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine A] [IsAffine B] (p : A ⟶ B) [Flat p] [Surjective p] (f : V ⟶ A) [IsQuasiAffineHom f] (D : Over.DescentDatum p (Over.mk f)) : CompactSpace V ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace V ∧ IsAffineHom (map f) ∧ IsOpenImmersion V.toSpecΓ ∧ ∃ E : Over.DescentDatum p (Over.mk (map f)), (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (a b : T ⟶ A) (h : a ≫ p = b ≫ p) (x : Over.mk a ⟶ Over.mk f), (E.transport a b h (x ≫ unit f)).left = (D.transport a b h x).left ≫ V.toSpecΓ) ∧ (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine T] (a b : T ⟶ A) [Flat a] [Flat b] (h : a ≫ p = b ≫ p), (transition p (Over.mk (map f)) E a b h).left = extendedTransition p f D a b h)
